item.title: St. Pio Devotions at Castleisland Parish Church Tues December 9th
item.description: St. Pio’s Healing Glove will be available for blessings at Castleisland Parish Church this Tuesday December 9th commencing at 7.30pm. Witness will be given by Ian O’Connell, Killarney and his theme is ‘Never let a stumble in life be the end of your story – let it be the beginning of a new and better Chapter’. Advertisement

item.title: Interagency training exercise involving gardaí taking place at Kerry Airport today
item.description: A training exercise involving gardaí and other primary response agencies is taking place at Kerry Airport today. The joint exercise between Kerry Airport, An Garda Síochána, and other primary response agencies takes place between 12:30 and 2:30pm. The live exercise will involve emergency services personnel, fire appliances, Garda vehicles and ambulances on site for the duration of the exercise. item.title: Radio Kerry and Fexco ask public to nominate Kerry Heroes 2025
item.description: Radio Kerry and Fexco are asking people to nominate who they consider to be the Kerry Heroes of 2025. These include individuals and groups who have shown outstanding community spirit, courage, and leadership over the last year in Kerry. There will be eight award recipients. item.title: 22 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry
item.description: There are 22 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry today. That’s according to figures from the Irish Nurses' and Midwives' Organisation. There are 17 patients waiting on trolleys in UHK’s ED today, while a further five people are on trolleys in wards in the hospital. Advertisement Nationally, there are 524 people waiting for a bed in hospitals today. University Hospital Limerick is the worst affected by overcrowding with 85 people waiting on trolleys there.

item.title: HSE confirms opening of additional beds at West Kerry Community Hospital
item.description: The HSE has confirmed that additional beds have opened at the West Kerry Community Hospital. Two beds opened at Ospidéal Pobail Corca Dhuibhne on Monday, with a further two beds expected to open in the coming week. In a statement to Radio Kerry, the HSE South West says there is no confirmed timeline for the opening of additional beds in Kenmare Community Nursing Unit. item.title: Castleisland business makes €4 million investment in renewable energy project
item.description: A Castleisland business has made a €4 million investment in a renewable energy project which will see their carbon emissions reduce by 95%. Tony Walsh of Walsh Colour Print and Educate.ie says the investment makes sense as it will cut their emissions and energy bills. He says their electricity costs rose from between €25,000 and €30,000 per month, up to €60,000. Advertisement They are installing a 950 kilowatt wind turbine and 1,200 kilowatts of solar panels. item.title: Kerry TD calls for state agencies to come together and ensure St Finan’s landbank isn’t sold to developers
item.description: A Kerry TD has said state bodies need to come together and ensure the St Finan’s landbank in Killarney is not sold to private developers. The HSE-owned, former mental health hospital, closed in 2012 and has lain idle since. The Land Development Agency has formally expressed an interest in acquiring half of the 13.2-hectare site, but not the hospital building itself as it’s not suitable for conversion to residential use. item.title: Amnesty International says charges against Kerry man on trial in Greece are baseless and must be dropped
item.description: Amnesty International says the charges against a Kerry man are baseless and must be dropped. Seán Binder, who grew up in Castlegregory, is one of 24 migrant rescue volunteers who stands trial in Greece today. He faces charges including membership of a criminal organsation, money laundering, and smuggling (facilitation of irregular entry) before the Court of Appeal of Lesvos. item.title: Finbarrs Aiming For 6th Munster Title As They Take On Dingle
item.description: Three Kerry clubs are in Munster final action this weekend. On Sunday, Dingle face Cork’s St Finbarr’s in the AIB Munster Senior Club Football Final. St Finbarr’s are chasing a sixth Munster title after winning their tenth Cork senior championship. Selector Ian Keery says the atmosphere in the club has been brilliant… Throw-in is at 1.30 in FBD Semple Stadium, Thurles.
